one_month_reasoning: The window runs to the Fri Oct 30 close, because Nov 1 is a Sunday. Two scheduled events fall inside it. (1) The Q3 2026 report, expected Wed Oct 21 after the close. Nasdaq/Zacks marks this date 'expected' and TI has not yet posted a webcast notice that I could find; it also fits TI's 2026 Wednesday cadence (Apr 22, Jul 22). The guide was $5.65-6.15B revenue and $2.23-2.57 EPS. Broad consensus is $2.42 for Q3 and $2.28 for Q4 (Yahoo/LSEG, 24 analysts), and every estimate revision in the last 30 days was upward. So the bar has risen, and the Q4 guide must beat a seasonal step-down that consensus already prices only lightly (Q4 $2.28 vs Q3 $2.42). Lead-time stretch and price increases argue for upside to the guide, while TI's conservative guiding and the July sell-the-news drop argue against chasing it. Net, I see no directional edge. (2) The $1.52 dividend goes ex on Oct 30, because the record date is Oct 30 and settlement is T+1. That mechanically lowers the Oct 30 close by about 0.5%; in round 1 I wrongly said it had no price effect. The distribution is therefore centred at $292.3 (spot less the dividend) with about 10.5% core monthly sigma (42%/3.5 shaded slightly, since part of the realized vol was the 2025 tariff shock) plus a 20%-weight fat-tail component at 20% sigma for an earnings-day move of about ±7-10%. The China anti-dumping probe is no longer treated as a window event: China committed on 2025-11-01 to terminate it, and no ruling has been found.

fair_value.method: The P/E leg values horizon NTM EPS of $10.50 at 23.5x, a modest premium to the 21.0x median of 10 peers on a single CY2027 basis: $247, weight 50%. The FCF-yield leg takes $9.76 a share of forward FCF ex-CHIPS at 3.5%, plus about $0.9 a share of CHIPS incentives still to be collected at the horizon: $280, weight 50%. The blend is about $264.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Horizon (Oct-2027) NTM EPS: 0.25 x CY27 $10.10 + 0.75 x CY28 $11.60 = $11.23. Less 4% for peak-cycle risk and the thin CY28 panel = $10.78, less $0.28 net GAAP Silicon Labs effect = $10.50. Multiple 23.5x. Value $247.

inputs_detail.input: Silicon Labs net GAAP EPS effect
inputs_detail.derivation: Financing and forgone interest on about $7.3B net outlay (33.4M SLAB shares x $231, less $0.40B SLAB cash, no SLAB debt; sources 13 and 15) is about $0.30-0.33 a share after tax. Against it, SLAB's 2028E NOPAT of $260M (about $0.28 a share; source 13) plus first-year synergies of about $100M pre-tax, from the $450M 3-year target (source 7), add about $0.38. Purchase-intangible amortization, assumed at about 45% of price over 8 years, is about $430M pre-tax and about $0.36 a share after tax. The net is about -$0.28. TI's 'accretive' claim excludes transaction-related costs (source 7).
See comps: one CY2027 consensus basis, with fiscal years calendarized; Zacks for US listings and MarketScreener for IFX, Renesas, Rohm and Melexis.

This is a 12% premium to the 21.0x median. It sits inside the interquartile range and below ADI's 25.0x. The premium rests only on persistent structural factors: owned 300mm capacity already built and depreciating (source 2), a balance sheet that stays about 1x EBITDA even after SLAB, and a policy of returning FCF. Lowest-in-set next-year growth (+15%) offsets most of that, so I do not go to ADI parity. See comps_summary.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: Horizon-NTM (Q4-27 to Q3-28): revenue about $24.5B x 45% CFO margin = $11.0B, less $2.0B capex, less $0.3B deal financing, plus $0.2B SLAB FCF = $8.9B ex-CHIPS. On 912M diluted shares that is $9.76, and at a 3.5% yield $279. Add about $0.9 a share of CHIPS incentives still to collect at the horizon, for $280.

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 had about $0.5B, which was wrong. I assume about $1.3B is collected before Oct-2027, leaving about $0.85B, or about $0.9 a share, added as a one-off rather than capitalized at the yield.
CY26 is about $21.1B (Q1 $4.07B, Q2 $5.46B, Q3 guide midpoint $5.9B, Q4 about $5.7B). Growth of about 10% in 2027 and about 8% in 2028 is consistent with consensus EPS of $10.10 and $11.60.
TTM is 44.6%. Higher fab utilization offsets the rising depreciation that is already in CFO.
2026 guide is $2-3B (H1-26 $1.19B), down from $4.9B. Management said capex declines as the 300mm build-out ends, so I take the low end for 2027-28.
Q2 diluted 920M and basic 913.2M (Jul 15). Buybacks are slow while SLAB cash competes, so I raised this from round 1's 905-915M view.

The TTM ex-CHIPS FCF yield is 2.0% ($5.36B on about $268B market cap) at peak capex. A normalized forward yield of 3.5% equals about 28.5x forward FCF. That is above my 23.5x P/E only because FCF per share ($9.76) is below the EPS used ($10.50). Raised from 3.25% in round 1 to stay consistent with the lower peer-median P/E.

bear.story: The 2026 shortage (price hikes on open POs, stretched lead times) turns into a double-ordering unwind in H1 2027. Customers digest inventory, utilization falls in the new 300mm fabs against about $2.2B+ of largely fixed depreciation, and CY28 EPS comes in at about $9.3 (GAAP, after SLAB amortization). At the 21.5x core peer median that is about $200. A China truce breakdown (anti-dumping duties) is a contributor in a minority of these paths, not a scheduled event.

base.story: The upcycle slows but continues. CY27 EPS is about $10.1 and horizon NTM GAAP EPS about $10.8-11. Capex at about $2B plus about $1B a year of CHIPS collections lifts FCF to about $9.5-10 a share, and SLAB closes in H1 2027 with net debt about $12-12.5B (about 1x EBITDA). The multiple compresses from 29x CY27 toward about 25-26x NTM, so price is roughly flat with the dividend as the return.

bull.story: Pricing plus data-center (2x y/y) and industrial demand push CY28 EPS to $12.5-13. Operating leverage on fixed fab cost lifts gross margin above 65%, FCF exceeds $11 a share, and the market keeps about 30x NTM, as it has during this upcycle.

comps_summary.peer_range: CY2027 P/E 14.6x (NXPI) to 47.6x (MPWR); interquartile about 18.3x (Renesas) to 25.0x (ADI). Without MPWR (the 9 IDM and broad-line names) the median is 20.7x, and on the supervisor's 7-name core set it is 20.7-21.0x. Forward EV/EBITDA runs 10.5x to 58.9x with a median of about 14.1x, but the basis is mixed (US names estimated as EV / [TTM EBITDA x (1 + 0.6 x CY27 EPS growth)]; non-US names from MarketScreener, calendarized), so it gets no weight.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: TXN trades at 29.1x CY27 LSEG consensus of $10.10 (29.9x on Zacks $9.84), a 39-42% premium to the 21.0x median. I apply 23.5x to horizon NTM EPS. That is a 12% premium, inside the interquartile range and below ADI's 25.0x.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Basis: every P/E uses calendar-2027 consensus EPS. US names use Nasdaq/Zacks yearly and quarterly consensus with fiscal years calendarized as shown; IFX, Renesas, ROHM and Melexis use MarketScreener, calendarized. stockanalysis 'Forward PE' was not used. For TXN itself I use the broader LSEG $10.10 rather than the stale Zacks figure; on Zacks the premium would be slightly larger. Peer set changes vs round 1: dropped LSCC, POWI, ALGM and SMTC (FPGA or niche high-growth names, 1-4 estimates) and DIOD (1 estimate); added Renesas, ROHM and Melexis (analog/MCU/power IDMs with the same end markets); kept MPWR as the one direct analog-power competitor, flagged. Premium: in round 1 I called 25x 'the peer median', which was wrong, because that median was inflated by non-comparables. My 23.5x is a premium and is argued as such, using only factors that persist through Oct-2027. (1) Cost structure: TI's 300mm capacity is already built (capex down from $4.9B to $2-3B, source 2), so its cost-per-unit advantage does not depend on a sell-side call and cannot erode within 12 months. (2) Balance sheet: net debt is about 1x EBITDA even after the $7.3B SLAB outlay (sources 2, 15), and $2.16B of CHIPS receivables are contracted (source 2). (3) Capital-return policy: dividend raised 7% for the 23rd straight year (source 3). Against these, TXN's next-year EPS growth (+15-19%) is the lowest of the 10, and its cyclicality (about -30% peak-to-trough revenue in 2022-24) matches peers. ADI has comparable margins and a higher growth rate at 25x, so TXN should not exceed ADI parity. That caps the defensible premium at about 10-15%; 23.5x sits there. Sell-side outperform calls are not used.

thesis_break_reason: $212 is 21x the $10.10 CY27 LSEG consensus, i.e. the 10-peer median with TI's premium fully gone, and about 19-20x horizon NTM EPS. It is 28% below spot, beyond about 0.75 sigma of ordinary annual noise on the core volatility. Trading there would most likely mean the 2026 shortage has flipped into a double-ordering or destocking correction that cuts CY27 EPS toward $8.5 (no growth over 2026), or that China has broken the Nov 2025 truce and imposed analog anti-dumping duties (22% of revenue is China-headquartered customers), or that the SLAB financing or integration has gone wrong. Round 1 was $215 on Zacks $9.84 and a mixed 22x; this re-bases to the corrected consensus and the single-basis median.

reasoning: Round-2 changes follow the supervisor's fact-checks, which I re-verified where it mattered. (a) Consensus: Yahoo/LSEG shows CY27 $10.10 from 28 analysts with 23 upward and 0 downward revisions in 30 days, and Q3 $2.42 / Q4 $2.28. Zacks' $9.84 panel is stale, so TXN is at 29.1x CY27. (b) CHIPS: $2.16B of incentives remain receivable (10-Q), not about $0.5B. I added about $0.9 a share left at the horizon as a one-off and kept recurring FCF ex-CHIPS. (c) SLAB: I added GAAP purchase amortization (about -$0.36 a share), giving a net deal effect of about -$0.28 a share on horizon EPS. (d) Comps: I rebuilt a 10-name single-basis CY27 set: dropped LSCC, POWI, ALGM, SMTC and DIOD; added Renesas, ROHM and Melexis from MarketScreener; kept MPWR flagged. The median is 21.0x, matching the supervisor's 21x core. My round-1 '25x = median' was mislabelled; I now apply 23.5x and argue it as a 12% premium, slightly below the supervisor's 24.5x because TXN's growth is the lowest in the set and ADI's comparable margins make ADI parity a ceiling, not a target. (e) The dividend goes ex Oct 30, inside the 1-month window. (f) The China AD probe is now a truce-breakdown tail risk, not a dated catalyst. Valuation: P/E $247 and FCF yield $280, blended 50/50 to $264. Round 1 was $282; the lower multiple outweighs the extra CHIPS cash. Distribution: fair value is 10% below spot, but earnings momentum is strong (all revisions up, lead times stretching), and multiples rarely de-rate fully inside 12 months mid-upcycle. So I set the 12-month median at $283, about 40% of the way from spot to fair value, below round 1's $292. The spread is a mixture: 85% lognormal at 32% sigma and 15% at 60% sigma. That is below the 42% realized vol, which was inflated by the 2025 tariff shock, with fat tails for a late-cycle semi. Checks: P(<212 thesis break) is about 20%; P(>=397) is 17%; scenarios $200/25%, $285/50%, $390/25% give a mean of about $290, against a ladder mean of about $298 (the fat right tail). Research was limited to 8 follow-up queries. TI has not confirmed the Q3 date, and Renesas/IFX EV/EBITDA come from MarketScreener on a different basis from the US estimates.
